name: Stars and Bars: # weak compositions of n into k parts = C(n+k-1, n)

insights: A weak composition f : Fin k → ℕ summing to n is the same data as a size-n multiset over Fin k: f records the multiplicity of each index, and Multiset.count recovers it. This is the precise content of the multichoose count C(n+k-1, n).
Mathlib has only the MULTISET form of stars and bars (Sym.card_sym_eq_choose : card (Sym α k) = C(card α + k - 1, k)); the function/tuple form C(n+k-1, n) and the bijection to it are not in Mathlib.
The Fintype instance on {f : Fin k → ℕ // ∑ i, f i = n} is NOT auto-derivable (codomain ℕ is infinite) and must be supplied via Fintype.ofEquiv through the bijection to Sym (Fin k) n.

Both bijection roundtrips reduce to Mathlib's count/replicate calculus: count_sum' + count_replicate + Fintype.sum_ite_eq' one way; nsmul_singleton + Finset.sum_subset + toFinset_sum_count_nsmul_eq the other.
